RiskContext.stablecoin: This is a stablecoin. Its issuer usually holds most of the supply and can mint and freeze coins — that is how it works, so concentration and owner powers are not counted here. The main risk of a stablecoin is the issuer's reserves, which cannot be checked on-chain.
RiskContext.cex_liquidity: Liquidity on centralised exchanges (order books, from CoinGecko) is counted, not only DEX pools.
RiskContext.exchange_holders: Exchange wallets are not counted as large holders: they hold coins for many customers.
RiskContext.skip_concentration: Holder concentration could not be assessed: recent transfers show only a small part of the supply, the rest sits in wallets that have not moved. This factor is not part of the score.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.privacy: How we handle data — see the privacy policy →
sections: What SpiderAML is

SpiderAML is a free information service. It collects what official sanctions lists and public databases say about crypto addresses and presents it in plain language. By using the site you agree to these terms.
Not a verdict and not an accusation

The risk score is produced automatically. It is not legal, tax or financial advice and not a statement that the owner of an address did anything unlawful. Addresses end up in databases by mistake, and new schemes may not be in any database yet. Low risk does not guarantee safety.
Data “as is”

We show third-party data as it was published and name the source next to every signal. We are not responsible for its completeness, accuracy or freshness, or for decisions made on the basis of the score. The sources and their terms are listed below.
Sanctions
A “sanctions list” mark only means the address appears in a list published by a regulator. Whether sanctions apply to you and how to comply is your responsibility; ask a lawyer if in doubt.
If an address is flagged by mistake

Tell us through the Report form (“This is a mistake”) or by email. We will review it and remove SpiderAML's own label if it is wrong. We cannot change official sanctions lists or other parties' databases, but we will tell you whom to contact.
Safe send
The Safe send section runs on the Arbitrum Sepolia testnet; the money there is not real. The SpiderSend contract never holds funds; your wallet makes the transfers and you confirm them yourself.
What is not allowed
Do not scrape the site automatically, work around rate limits, disrupt the service, or present a SpiderAML score as an official decision of a regulator.
Changes
We may update the service and these terms; the date of the last change is shown at the top.

Privacy.title: Privacy
sections: In short

There is no sign-up. We do not ask for your name, email or phone, do not store IP addresses and use no advertising cookies. We turn on Google Analytics only if you agree in the banner; until then nothing from Google is loaded.
Visit statistics

To see what is used, we record: which page was opened and what was clicked; the site you came from (domain only) or a link tag such as ?src=telegram; the device type (phone or computer); the country, as reported by Cloudflare. A visitor is identified for one day by a hash of a random “salt”, the IP address and the browser; the salt is deleted the next day, so visits on different days cannot be linked and the record cannot identify a person. Records older than 13 months are deleted automatically.
Google Analytics (only with your consent)

If you click “Accept”, Google Analytics 4 is switched on. It sets cookies, infers an approximate location and device type, and sends Google which pages were opened and when. The page address is sent without its parameters, so the addresses you check never reach Google. Advertising features and personalisation are off. You can withdraw consent at any time with the “Cookie settings” button at the bottom of the page: Google then stops receiving data and its cookies are deleted.
Checked addresses

When you check an address or a token we store the address, the network and the result, to see what people look for most. Crypto addresses are public; the record is not tied to your identity. To run the check our server sends the address (not your data) to external services: GoPlus, Zerion, CoinGecko, Etherscan and a blockchain node provider.
Address reports

The Report form stores the address, network, category, your description and the link. We do not ask for contact details — please do not put personal data in the description. Only the SpiderAML team sees the report; its status opens through a secret link that only you receive.
Cookies and browser storage

The site remembers your chosen language in one cookie (NEXT_LOCALE) for a year, and your answer about analytics in the browser's local storage. If you allowed Google Analytics, Google sets its own cookies (_ga…); if you decline we delete them. In Safe send your browser remembers that a wallet was connected; this stays on your device. We never receive your wallet, keys or signatures.
Who else handles traffic

The site runs behind Cloudflare (protection and delivery) on a Hetzner server in the European Union. Cloudflare sees technical request data under its own privacy policy. If you agreed to analytics, Google also receives data about your visit.
Your rights
You can ask us to delete a report you sent or ask about your data — write to us. Since we do not know who you are, include the report's status link.

Consent.title: Cookies and analytics
Consent.text: We would like to count visits with Google Analytics: it sets cookies and sends data to Google. Nothing from Google is loaded until you agree. Only the pages you open are sent, never the addresses you check.
